Synopsis:
    Following a catastrophic glacial flood that killed 1,114+ people and left ~4,000 missing along the Nepal-China border, Nepal is urgently rebuilding an early-warning system at Timure (Rasuwa district). The plan involves seismic sensors, cameras, and a VSAT satellite link to maintain connectivity when mobile networks fail — a critical gap exposed when the flood knocked out four gauging stations. Near-term instability remains a concern as the terrain is still adjusting post-event, and two barrier lakes are being monitored. Nepal is also pushing for deeper real-time data-sharing cooperation with China on glacier and water-level monitoring.
